title: nf-core/deepmutscan pipeline parameters
description: Processing and analysis of deep mutational scanning (DMS) data from shotgun and amplicon sequencing: read alignment, variant counting, sequencing-error correction, library QC and fitness estimation

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a samplesheet with information about the sequencing libraries in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 5 columns (`sample`, `type`, `replicate`, `file1`, `file2`) and a header row. See [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/deepmutscan/usage#samplesheet-input).

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

reference_options.title: Reference and library options
reference_options.description: The reference sequence, the mutagenised reading frame and the programmed codon library.

fasta.description: Path to a FASTA file with the wildtype reference sequence of the mutagenised gene (exactly one sequence).
fasta.help_text: The reference may include flanking sequence around the open reading frame (set with `--reading_frame`). A BWA index is built automatically and saved under `intermediate_files/bwa/`.

reading_frame.description: Nucleotide coordinates of the mutagenised open reading frame within the reference FASTA, in the format 'start-stop' (1-based, inclusive), e.g. '352-1383'.

mutagenesis_type.description: Codons programmed at each position of the library. When using 'custom', also provide '--custom_codon_library'.

custom_codon_library.description: Path to a .csv file defining a custom codon library. Required when '--mutagenesis_type custom' is set. Provide either one global comma-separated list of codons without header (e.g. 'AAA,AAC,AAG'), or a position-wise list with a header line containing 'Position', followed by one row per codon position with the position and its allowed codons (e.g. '1,ACG,AAA,ACA' and '2,AAA,TTT,ACA' on separate lines).

variant_counting_options.title: Variant counting options
variant_counting_options.description: Base-quality and read-edge filters of the variant counter.

base_qual.description: Minimum base quality (Phred) for a mismatch to be counted as a mutation, and for a base to contribute to sequencing coverage.

min_flank.description: Minimum distance (nt) a mutation or covered base must be from a read edge; also excludes those bases from coverage. Set to 0 to disable edge trimming.

save_bam.description: Publish the sorted, indexed BAM of every library to intermediate_files/bam_files/sorted/.
save_bam.help_text: The variant counter reads the filtered alignments straight from the merge-align stream and needs no BAM, so without this option none is written. With it, the same alignments are also coordinate-sorted and indexed in the MERGE_ALIGN_COUNT task (several GB per full-size run). Leave it off unless you want to inspect the alignments: the count tables carry everything downstream steps use.

error_correction_options.title: Sequencing-error correction options
error_correction_options.description: Correction of single-nucleotide variant counts for sequencing errors.

error_correction.description: Sequencing-error correction of variant counts. 'false_doubles' (default) estimates the error rate of every single-nucleotide variant from reads that carry it together with a nearby programmed multi-nucleotide codon variant; 'wildtype' subtracts the background measured by additional deep sequencing of the unmutated template (requires samplesheet rows with type 'wildtype'); 'none' disables correction.

false_doubles_method.description: Estimator used by the false-doubles correction. 'eb' (default) is an empirical-Bayes estimate: each variant's error rate is shrunk towards the mean of its class (see `false_doubles_prior`) in proportion to how little evidence it has, so sparsely observed variants get a stable rate. 'mle' is the per-variant maximum-likelihood rate F/M, which is zero for every variant without an observed false double and therefore depth-sensitive. Only applies when error_correction = 'false_doubles'.

false_doubles_prior.description: Prior classes of the empirical-Bayes estimator. 'trinucleotide_context' (default) shrinks each variant towards the mean of its trinucleotide context (substitution type plus both flanking bases, 96 classes), which is itself shrunk towards its substitution type; 'substitution_type' shrinks towards the mean of the six pyrimidine-folded substitution types only. Only applies when false_doubles_method = 'eb'.

false_doubles_pooling.description: Libraries that share one error-rate estimate in the false-doubles correction. 'all' (default) pools every non-wildtype library of a `sample`; 'replicates' pools the replicates of each `sample` and `type`; 'none' estimates every library on its own. Pooled libraries sum their false-double evidence per variant, the rates are estimated once and each library is corrected at its own coverage. Pooling assumes one error process across the pool, i.e. libraries prepared, processed and sequenced together. Use 'replicates' if conditions or sorting bins were amplified or sequenced separately, as a pool with different error rates gets a confidently wrong common rate. Per-library estimates are always reported next to the pooled ones. Wildtype-template libraries are never pooled or corrected.

max_FDdist.description: Maximum distance, in codons, between a single-nucleotide variant and the programmed multi-nucleotide variant used as its anchor in the false-doubles correction.
max_FDdist.help_text: With --min_FDdist this bounds the anchors each variant's error rate is read from: min_FDdist < distance <= max_FDdist. Anchors farther away are observed on fewer and fewer molecules, because both changes must sit on one fragment, and the evidence they carry is biased as well as thin: estimated from anchors 40-60 codons away, the error rate of the rarest quartile of variants runs about three times the rate measured on a matched wildtype template, while abundant variants are unaffected - an additive background of order 1e-5, consistent with PCR template switching, which the genuine-double subtraction does not remove. Swept from 15 to 120 codons on five libraries, 40 gives the best agreement with wildtype-template sequencing; below 25 the evidence collapses and the estimate falls back on the class prior. Raise it only to look at the anchor profile itself, and lower it if the sequencing fragments are shorter than about 250 bp.

min_FDdist.description: Minimum distance, in codons, between a single-nucleotide variant and the programmed multi-nucleotide variant used as its anchor in the false-doubles correction.
min_FDdist.help_text: Within one mutagenesis primer's footprint the false doubles are dominated by that primer's own recurrent synthesis or sequencing errors: they travel with the anchor by construction, so they are not the per-site error the model estimates, and they inflate the rate of variants that happen to lie near an anchor. A genuine second primer integration is near-impossible at those distances, because the two footprints would clash. The default of 13 codons covers the footprint of a typical nicking-mutagenesis primer (about 40 bp either side of the randomised codon); set it to 0 for libraries made without nicking mutagenesis, such as a tile synthesis, which has no primer footprint: there the exclusion removes evidence without removing an artefact. The excluded region is still measured and reported.

subtract_genuine_doubles.description: Subtract genuine double mutants from the false-double evidence before estimating the error rate.
subtract_genuine_doubles.help_text: Two mutagenesis primers can integrate into the same molecule, so a read can carry a programmed anchor next to a variant without any sequencing error. Those reads are in F and are not error. The rate of genuine co-integration relative to independence, kappa(d), is measured on reads carrying two programmed multi-nucleotide variants - which no sequencing error can create - pooled over the libraries of each pool and taken at each codon distance, smoothed over neighbouring distances. Each variant's expected genuine-double reads are then G = f * sum_p kappa(d) m_p, and the estimator splits F between error and genuine doubles by expectation-maximisation. Turning this off (false) estimates the rate from the raw false-double reads, which overstates it, most of all for abundant variants in libraries with widely spaced primers.

skip_error_signatures.description: Skip the mutational-signature fit of the error spectrum (false-doubles correction only).
skip_error_signatures.help_text: With false-doubles correction, the 96-channel error spectrum of every pool is fitted to a candidate set of mutational signatures: the false-double error rates, and, if the sample has a wildtype-template library, the wildtype-template error rates and the excess of the former over the latter. The fit is two-stage non-negative least squares with a site bootstrap; results appear in the error-correction report and in error_signatures/. Reporting only: the correction itself does not use it.

error_signatures_candidates.description: Candidate signatures for the error-spectrum fit: CSV with a `channel` column in COSMIC notation (e.g. A[C>A]A, 96 rows) and one column per signature, on GRCh37 trinucleotide composition.
error_signatures_candidates.help_text: The default holds the 19 COSMIC v3.4 SBS signatures flagged as possible sequencing or library artefacts (SBS27, SBS43, SBS45-SBS60, SBS95) plus DNA-damage chemistry that can act on DNA in vitro: the unrepaired and repaired FFPE signatures of Guo et al. (2022, Nat Commun 13:4487), SBS30 and SBS18. Clock-like signatures are excluded by default. Leave unset to use it (assets/error_signatures/candidate_signatures_GRCh37.csv).

error_signatures_max_cosine.description: Signatures whose cosine similarity to an already selected signature is at or above this value are not added in the forward selection of the error-spectrum fit.

error_signatures_bootstraps.description: Site bootstrap resamples for the candidate screen and the exposure intervals of the error-spectrum fit.

error_signatures_genuine_doubles.description: Remove the expected genuine double-mutant reads from the false doubles before forming the excess error spectrum.
error_signatures_genuine_doubles.help_text: Reads carrying two programmed multi-nucleotide codon variants are genuine double mutants (synthesis, PCR chimeras). Their rate relative to the variants' library frequencies (kappa) is measured per library in the evidence step and used to subtract the expected genuine doubles from each single-nucleotide variant's false doubles.

library_qc_options.title: Library QC options
library_qc_options.description: Positional coverage and count profiles, and sequencing-depth rarefaction.

sliding_window_size.description: Sliding-window size (in codons) used to smooth the positional coverage and count profiles in the library QC plots.

aimed_cov.description: Targeted number of counts per amino acid variant. Used to draw the sequencing coverage that would be required (assuming an even spread) in the positional coverage plots and the run report.

run_seqdepth.description: Estimate sequencing-depth saturation of every library by closed-form hypergeometric rarefaction (on by default).

fitness_options.title: Fitness estimation options
fitness_options.description: Fitness estimation from matched input and output libraries, optional additional estimators and the 3D variant effect inspection tool.

fitness.description: Estimate variant fitness from matched 'input' and 'output' libraries of each sample, using the default log-ratio estimator.

min_counts.description: Minimum number of reads a variant needs in every 'input' replicate to receive a fitness estimate. Applied to the default estimator, DiMSum ('--fitnessMinInputCountAll') and mutscan. Variant counting, error correction and library QC are not filtered.

output_pseudocount.description: Pseudocount for 'output' replicates in which a variant observed in the input was not detected (dropouts), so that strongly depleted variants still receive a finite fitness value. Applied to the default estimator and DiMSum ('--fitnessDropoutPseudocount'). Set to 0 to disable; dropout variants then receive no fitness estimate in that replicate.

dimsum.description: Additionally estimate fitness with DiMSum (Faure et al., 2020). Requires '--fitness'.

dimsum_error_model.description: Fit DiMSum's error model ('--fitnessErrorModel'): replicate-specific error terms and normalisation, estimated by bootstrapping. Needs at least 30 variants per replicate (90 for three replicates) that pass '--min_counts' and are observed in every replicate; set to false for sparse libraries.
dimsum_error_model.help_text: With the error model, DiMSum's fitness sigmas combine count-based and replicate errors, fitted on the variants that are well covered in every input and output replicate (at least 10 per fitted parameter, i.e. 30 per replicate). Without it, the sigmas are count-based only. The fit runs on one CPU so that its bootstrap resamples, and hence its numbers, do not depend on the CPUs a task is given.

mutscan.description: Additionally estimate variant enrichment with edgeR and limma-voom, following mutscan's analysis (Soneson et al., 2023). Requires '--fitness'.

pdb.description: Optional wildtype 3D structure (PDB). When supplied together with `--fitness`, an interactive variant effect inspection tool (self-contained HTML) is built that projects fitness, counts and error-correction biases onto the structure.
pdb.help_text: Use a crystal structure, an AlphaFold DB model, or any precomputed PDB whose sequence matches the wildtype ORF. Structure prediction (nf-core/proteinfold) is not wired in this release.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

co2_location.description: Electricity Maps zone code of the compute site for the carbon-footprint estimate (e.g. `ES`, `DE`, `US-CAL-CISO`).
co2_location.help_text: Used by the nf-co2footprint plugin to pick the carbon intensity of the local grid (yearly 2024 average without an API key). Unset, the plugin uses a global average. Best set once in a site profile or custom config.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
